title: Extending Noisy-Leakage Proofs Beyond I.S.W.
summary: The direct noisy-leakage proof covers only I.S.W.

formal_statement.body: The direct noisy-leakage security proof currently covers only the I.S.W. masking scheme, whereas the generic approach through the probing model can cover any masking scheme. The unresolved theorem-extension problem is to determine whether the direct proof can be generalized from the I.S.W. multiplication gadget to other masking gadgets, in particular table-based masking schemes, and to establish the resulting security bounds in the noisy leakage model. This target is especially relevant because table-based masking schemes are known to be efficiently secure in the probing model but much less so in the noisy leakage model.

scope.domain: Side-channel analysis of masking gadgets, including I.S.W. and table-based schemes, in probing and noisy-leakage models.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the direct I.S.W. proof extends to other masking gadgets, especially table-based schemes, and establish the resulting noisy-leakage security bounds.

citations.label: Prou? & Rivain’s Formal Security Proof of Masking, Revisited: Tight Bounds in the Noisy Leakage Model

progress.summary: The source contrasts a direct noisy-leakage proof limited to I.S.W. with a generic probing-model approach that can cover any masking scheme. It presents extension to other gadgets, particularly table-based masking, as an open avenue for improvement.
citation_labels: Loïc Masure et al., Prou? & Rivain’s Formal Security Proof of Masking, Revisited: Tight Bounds in the Noisy Leakage Model
